name: Vulnerability Scan Result and Remediation Tracking
description: Scanner output for a scan executed during the examination period, together with the asset coverage basis for that scan and the tracking records showing how identified vulnerabilities were driven to closure or formally accepted.

expected_content.element: Scan execution date, scanner identity, and scan configuration or profile
expected_content.why: Places the scan within the period and establishes what kind of scan was run.
Coverage is the substance of the control; results are meaningless without knowing what was covered.

expected_content.element: Authoritative asset inventory for the same date, with reconciliation against the scanned list
expected_content.why: Demonstrates the scan scope matched the environment. Unreconciled scope is the most common defect in this evidence.

expected_content.element: Findings with severity ranking and affected asset
expected_content.why: Drives the remediation timeframe and enables SLA assessment.

expected_content.element: Whether scanning was authenticated or unauthenticated
expected_content.why: Unauthenticated scans systematically understate exposure and change the conclusion that can be drawn.

expected_content.element: Remediation tracking records showing detection date, target date, and actual closure date per finding
expected_content.why: Operating effectiveness rests on timeliness, not on the scan having run.

expected_content.element: Documented, authorised, time-bounded risk acceptance for any finding not remediated within its timeframe
expected_content.why: Distinguishes a governed exception from an unaddressed vulnerability.

expected_content.element: Rescan or verification confirming the vulnerability is no longer present
expected_content.why: Ticket closure alone does not demonstrate the vulnerability was fixed.

source_system_examples: Container image scanner in the build pipeline

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default of one monthly cadence plus a 15-day grace window. Not an audit rule.

redaction_guidance: Unremediated vulnerability detail is directly exploitable. Restrict distribution, and never attach raw scan output to a customer-facing report.
Exclude proof-of-concept payloads and exploit detail from any shared artifact.
Hostnames and IPs may be tokenised provided reconciliation to the asset inventory remains possible.
retention_guidance: Retain scan output and tracking records for the full examination period; retention shorter than the period leaves an untestable interval.

validation_rules.rule: Scan results exist for every scheduled scan interval within the examination period, with no unexplained gaps.
Scanned assets reconcile to the authoritative asset inventory for the same date.
Findings were closed within the remediation timeframe the organization defined for their severity.
Every finding exceeding its timeframe carries a documented, authorised, time-bounded risk acceptance.
Output is a scanner-generated export rather than a manually compiled summary.
Scanned assets fall within the declared system boundary for the examination.

common_issues.issue: Scan target list is static while the environment is dynamic, so newly provisioned assets are never scanned.
common_issues.impact: Coverage silently degrades over the period without anyone detecting it.

common_issues.issue: Findings remain open well past the organization's stated remediation timeframe with no risk acceptance.
common_issues.impact: The organization is not meeting the commitment it defined for itself, which is how operating effectiveness is judged.

common_issues.issue: Only host scanning is performed; container images and third-party dependencies are unscanned.
common_issues.impact: A material portion of the attack surface is outside the control.

common_issues.issue: Summary dashboard screenshot provided instead of the underlying findings and tracking records.
common_issues.impact: Neither coverage nor timeliness can be assessed from a summary.

source_refs.supports: Scope reconciliation and SLA-adherence expectations, and the common issues list.
Freshness window, sensitivity classification, and redaction guidance.

notes: The criteria do not prescribe scan frequency or remediation timeframes. DriftGuard assesses adherence to the timeframes the organization itself defined, which is the basis on which operating effectiveness is judged.
Scanner output is system-generated; risk-acceptance records within the same package are human-generated and are weighted separately.
Backfilled with evidence_role and origin in the CC6 phase (schema 0.2.0). Content otherwise unchanged.
